status: Adopted 2026-10-25 (AQ-042): pooled revision option (ii) cap+A2, configuration A (California in the common level); Madison on the observed Madison-like path. Revised 2026-10-26 (AQ-043): lower = mean of Rhode Island and Oregon; Milwaukee at its measured 2022-2025 rate; reference line = median of all 8 statewide-law states
units: second-home permits on single-family lots per 1,000 one-unit detached homes per year

area_levels.basis: pooled two-stage model across California (cap of 2 ADUs per parcel plus the A2 multifamily parcel rule, AQ-041), seven statewide-law states and five cities, with the vacant-lot new-house factor x(1 - 0.049) on non-California series (AQ-039) and Minneapolis x(1 - 0.127); written by scripts/run_pooled_revision.py (docs/gate3/POOLED_REVISION.md)

madison_floor.units: second-home permits on single-family lots per 1,000 one-unit detached homes per year; applied to every area and path by the engine (AQ-024)

g3f_revision_2026_10_25.basis: Madison 2022-2025: 40 second-home units / 213.168 thousand home-years (53,292 one-unit detached homes x 4 years) = 0.1876, divided by 0.8 = 0.2345 (docs/gate3/POOLED_REVISION.md)

level_from.rule: each area's central level x (mean of the states' stage-2 levels at a typical place, law in force 4+ years / the common level of the same fit); Rhode Island 0.6214 and Oregon 0.6826, mean 0.6520, / common level 1.0035 = 0.6497

lower.basis: Like the slowest statewide-law states (owner decision 2026-10-26, AQ-043): the mean of Rhode Island's (0.6214) and Oregon's (0.6826) stage-2 levels, 0.6520 permits per 1,000 single-family homes per year at a typical place with the law in force 4+ years, = 0.6497 of the common level 1.0035. Every area's central level is multiplied by 0.6497 (same within-state differences). Ramp: the pooled ramp recomputed for this level the way the central and upper ramps were (homes-weighted, on the Gate 3 current-law rates), not Oregon's observed ramp. Replaces the 10th percentile of the between-state spread (factor 1/1.885), now a sensitivity case.
lower.label: Sluggish adoption
lower.info: Like the average of the two slowest statewide-law states, Rhode Island and Oregon.

central.basis: Like a typical statewide-law state: pooled revision (ii) configuration A central; ramp from the pooled year terms
central.label: Like a typical statewide-law state

upper.basis: Strong adoption: pooled revision (ii) configuration A, 90th percentile of the between-state spread (factor 1.89). The high end of what statewide-law states have reached; only California has gone higher.
upper.label: Strong adoption
upper.info: The high end of what statewide-law states have reached; only California has gone higher.

madison_like_path.units: second-home permits on single-family lots per 1,000 one-unit detached homes per year, forecast years 1-5 (2027-2031); already ramped, so the engine applies no ramp on top
madison_like_path.source: reference/madison_like_median_path.csv, group 'WA+OR Madison-like (main)': median of 9 Washington and Oregon Madison-like cities in years 1-3 and 4 Oregon cities in years 4-5 (docs/gate3/MADISON_LIKE_CITIES.md)
madison_like_path.basis: Owner decision 2026-10-25 (AQ-040 follow-up, AQ-042): Madison, the only Wisconsin place meeting the Madison-like definition (incorporated; 20,000-120,000 one-unit detached homes; median value $250,000-$500,000; not the largest city), follows the observed Madison-like path instead of its pooled level.

statewide_adoption_line: Adopted 2026-10-26 (AQ-043): median observed statewide rate across all 8 statewide-law states, California included (cap+A2 counts, 2020 = year 1; the other seven x0.951 for vacant-lot ADUs), years 1-4 (2027-2030) where data exist; year 5 (2031) has only California, so the year-4 median is carried forward and flagged. Points: reference/scenario_options_reference_points.csv; computed by scripts/run_adu_model.py into reference/adu_model_reference_lines.csv and adu_model_reference_line_by_year.csv. The 7-state line (California out; reference/pooled_revision_adoption_line.csv) is kept as an alternative row.
notes: Uniform 'level' (the Madison floor) applies only where an area has no model level. The Madison floor is set once, in madison_floor (in_use selects the variant; every path and script reads it via missing_middleware.model.params.madison_floor). area_paths replaces an area's level and ramp with an explicit observed path (engine.run area_paths). The California ramp is not applied on top of the pooled ramp. Path-specific ramps reproduce the pooled model's direct totals (each path scales the whole rate path); rounded to 4 decimals. The lower's level_from rule is applied by scripts/run_adu_model.py (load_area_levels); the stored factor and ramp are checked against the files there.
